title: TE Craig Sheppard v. Highlands Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint sustained. Issue 1: Yes—Presbytery erred at its November 9, 2021 meeting by approving Judicial Commission recommendations that conflated judicial and pastoral procedures and failed to institute timely process after the Commission found a strong presumption of guilt under BCO 31-2. Issue 2: Yes—Presbytery failed to institute process within the one-year requirement of BCO 32-20, and Presbytery is debarred from prosecuting any of the allegations embraced by the subject matter of the case. The adopted judgment ordered no remand.
first_summary: The SJC sustained TE Craig Sheppard's complaint against Highlands Presbytery. It held that Presbytery erred when its Judicial Commission found a strong presumption of guilt but instead of instituting process under BCO 31-2 directed a pastoral reconciliation process and conditioned later process on reconciliation. It also held that BCO 32-20's one-year time bar had run and that the 2022 amendment did not apply retroactively, so Presbytery is debarred from prosecuting the allegations. Three commissioners dissented, chiefly disputing the BCO 32-20 ruling.
summary: The SJC sustained TE Craig Sheppard's complaint against Highlands Presbytery. It held that Presbytery erred when its Judicial Commission found a strong presumption of guilt but, instead of instituting process under BCO 31-2, directed pastoral reconciliation and conditioned later process on its success; that motion also impaired the accused's right against self-incrimination. It further held that BCO 32-20's one-year time bar had run and that the 2022 amendment did not apply retroactively, so Presbytery is debarred from prosecuting the allegations. Four commissioners dissented, disputing the BCO 32-20 ruling.

sources.supports: Adopted decision, issues, judgments, BCO 31-2 and BCO 32-20 reasoning, debarment relief, and 16–4 approval vote with dissents and recusals.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2022-04, Sheppard v. Highlands Presbytery, Decision on Complaint dated October 20, 2022, in the 50th General Assembly (2023) minutes. The panel’s proposed decision was drafted by RE Steve Dowling and unanimously approved by the panel; the SJC approved it as amended 16–4, with three recused and one absent (lines 14–18, 205–212).
evidence_notes.dispute: TE Craig Sheppard, former pastor of Arden Presbyterian Church, complained against Highlands Presbytery’s November 9, 2021 action after allegations concerning his character and conduct arose following his departure for Indonesia. The stated issues were whether Presbytery erred by conflating judicial and pastoral procedures and failing to institute timely process after a strong presumption of guilt, and whether BCO 32-20 barred prosecution (lines 22–26, 88–104).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Both issues were answered Yes (lines 108–114). Under BCO 31-2, process is mandatory once a court finds a strong presumption of guilt; the Judicial Commission found such a presumption but instead directed pastoral reconciliation and conditioned later process on its success, which the SJC held improper and harmful to the accused’s right against self-incrimination (lines 120–172). Under BCO 32-20, the alleged offense occurred in 2017, the Session knew in July 2019, Presbytery knew in July 2020, and process had not begun by January 6, 2022; the SJC held timely prosecution should have begun by July 2021 and that the 2022 BCO 32-20 amendment did not apply retroactively (lines 176–203). Presbytery was debarred from further prosecution (lines 114, 203).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted decision drew dissenting opinions on Issue 2. RE Jim Eggert, joined by RE S. Duncan and RE Donahoe, would have remanded for process and argued former BCO 32-20 was a goad to timely action, not a statute of limitations. RE Howie Donahoe, joined in part by RE S. Duncan, argued BCO 32-20 did not apply because the matter was not shown to be a case of scandal or recently flagrant, and challenged the standard of review and stare decisis analysis (lines 224–232, 497–515, 559–587). RE Waters, RE Kooistra, and RE Terrell recused (lines 212–220).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate decision is incorporated by reference in the adopted judgment. The majority cites SJC 2016-05, Troxell v. Presbytery of the Southwest, as precedent for BCO 32-20 timeliness and states this case cannot be decided differently; the dissent also cites Ganzel and other prior cases, but their full texts are not included in this source (lines 178–201, 291–299).

source_limits: The source reproduces the SJC decision and dissenting opinions as printed in the GA minutes. It does not include the full lower-court record or the full text of cited prior decisions and BCO amendments.
benchmark_examples: C01. 1978-02: Allin et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery — preserve both successful procedural grounds and an unsuccessful merits claim; mixed disposition and remand.
C20. 2016-13: Daniels et al. v. Nashville Presbytery — an unexplained adopted disposition must remain unexplained; separate dissent is not the adopted ruling.

score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the rule that a strong presumption of guilt requires process and that pastoral reconciliation cannot be conditioned to reset the BCO 32-20 timeline.
